validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: one of the best-documented rows in this batch. Independently corroborated across FERC's own docket notices (Federal Register 2015-07-16 notice of application and 2015-08-04 EA notice, docket CP15-523), NGI trade press (2015-12-17 FERC-approval article and 2017-04-06 in-service article), the company's own Business Wire release (2017-04-04, read via Wayback since the live americanmidstream.com investor-relations URL now 404s), Pipeline & Gas Journal (2017-03), and the CURRENT operator's own site (blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission) plus a December-2025 PHMSA federal inspection document. All confirm a real, FERC-regulated interstate natural-gas transmission pipeline under NGA section 7(c) certificate CP15-523 -- Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission both correctly recorded (Black Bear's own site explicitly labels it 'FERC-Regulated Interstate'). LENGTH: GEM's 52.00 mi matches FERC's application filing (51.97 mi), both NGI articles (51.96 mi), and Black Bear's current listing ('52 miles'). The company's own April-2017 press release rounds up to '55-mile' -- an outlier against four more precise, converging sources, not chased further (possibly includes the 0.5-mi Vidalia lateral plus some interconnect tie-in footage). DIAMETER: 12 in confirmed unanimously (FERC x2, NGI x2, Business Wire, Black Bear's current site: '12 inch'). LOCATION: Winnsboro, LA -> Natchez, MS confirmed by both Federal Register notices and both NGI articles (route detail: Franklin, Catahoula, Concordia parishes LA, under the Mississippi River, into Adams County MS). START DATE 2017-04: Business Wire announced in-service 'today' dated April 4, 2017; NGI's April 6, 2017 article independently cites a FERC letter order dated March 29, 2017 authorizing in-service -- both agree on April 2017. CONSTRUCTION YEAR 2016: consistent with the record (FERC certificate granted Dec 2015 -> $60M senior secured notes issued Sept 2016 per Business Wire, explicitly to finance the project -> in-service April 2017) though no single source states 'construction began in 2016' verbatim -- treat the added ref as contextual/medium support, not a direct quote. DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against all 49 other rows in the 50-row roster -- no overlap; Winnsboro(LA)-Natchez(MS) is a unique corridor unlike any other row. For the record only (not an action item on this row): the *historic* ~370-mile 'Midla' pipeline system (Desiard Compressor Station, Ouachita Parish LA, to Scottlandville, East Baton Rouge Parish LA) that the Natchez Pipeline REPLACED was approved for abandonment by FERC in the same December-2015 order (settlement docket RP14-638) -- that old system is a separate, since-abandoned pipeline, is not one of the 50 rows in this roster, and I have not checked whether it still carries a stale 'operating' row elsewhere in GEM outside this batch's scope. CITATION COVERAGE: opened all 6 harvested wiki citations for this row -- the americanmidstream.com press release is dead (404, no Wayback snapshot exists for that exact investor-relations URL either); the FracTracker map and eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php are both live but are generic navigation/map pages that never name this pipeline, so not citable per the aggregate-source rule; Business Wire, the NGI in-service article, and the Federal Register notice are all live, all name the pipeline, and are used above. Beyond the harvested pool I independently found and used 6 more sources (a second Federal Register notice, a second NGI article, PGJ, Black Bear's current pipeline listing, PHMSA's Dec-2025 inspection document, and pipelinesafetyinfo.com's operator safety flyer) -- 9 total sources opened and read for this row.

validity.recommendation: Update Owner1 off 'Third Coast Midstream LLC' -- that entity sold this pipeline's parent business (Black Bear Transmission, 7 laterals incl. Midla) to Basalt Infrastructure Partners in 2019/2020, and Basalt in turn sold Black Bear Transmission Opco, LLC to Enstor Pipeline Holdings, LLC, closing November 13, 2025. I could not find a public disclosure of the exact post-close legal-entity name/percentage split, so I'm not proposing a specific replacement Owner1 string -- route to Update to pull the FERC Form 2/NPMS operator-ID record or a post-close Enstor filing for the precise current owner of record. See the paired Operator fill below for the operating-subsidiary name, which IS well sourced.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Owner1='Third Coast Midstream LLC' (100%) is several ownership changes stale. Chain, reconstructed from independent reporting: (1) at April-2017 in-service, the owner was American Midstream Partners LP (NYSE: AMID) per its own Business Wire release. (2) American Midstream was taken private by ArcLight Capital Partners in July 2018 and renamed Third Coast Midstream LLC (NGI, Oct 21, 2019: 'Third Coast, formerly American Midstream Partners LP, was taken private by ArcLight Capital Partners LLC in July') -- presumably the origin of GEM's current value, correct as of 2018-2019 but not current. (3) A fund managed by Basalt Infrastructure Partners II GP Ltd. agreed in October 2019 to acquire Third Coast's natural-gas-transmission business -- 'seven natural gas laterals span roughly 550 miles ... connected to eight pipelines that feed supply to consumers in Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mis[sissippi]' (NGI, Oct 2019) -- and rebranded it Black Bear Transmission LLC; Black Bear's own site confirms Midla is one of its currently-listed pipelines (blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission: 'Midla: FERC-Regulated Interstate, 52 miles, 12 inch ... 48 MDth/d capacity ... 12 delivery points, 2 receipt points' -- an exact spec match to this row, confirming Black Bear's 'Midla' entry IS the Natchez Pipeline). (4) Black Bear Transmission Opco, LLC was acquired by Enstor Pipeline Holdings, LLC, closing November 13, 2025 (multiple trade-press reports, e.g. Pipeline & Gas Journal and Business Wire, Nov 2025) -- the most recent ownership event on record. I flag this as attribution concern rather than a fill because Owner1 already carries a value (this is a correction, not a blank), and standing rule 'never auto-apply a reference value' means a research judgment on the exact current legal owner needs Update's normal source-search, not a live overwrite here. Second-source note: the Basalt (2019) and Enstor (2025) transaction articles I found describe the whole Black-Bear/Third-Coast portfolio and never name 'Midla' specifically, so per the relevance rule they aren't staged as proposed_refs for this row -- I only cite the row-specific blackbearllc.com listing and the operator-identity docs below as verified refs; the transaction articles are background only, described here for Update's benefit but not staged as citations.

validity.recommendation: SegmentCost=$66,200,000 matches only the PRE-CONSTRUCTION FERC application estimate (2015). Two independent 2017 sources (the company's own Business Wire release and NGI's independent reporting) instead state the actual built/financed project cost was $60 million. Recommend Update revise SegmentCost to 60,000,000 USD citing the actual project financing, and treat the $66.2M figure as a superseded pre-construction estimate (note it in ResearcherNotes rather than silently dropping it).
validity.researcher_notes: The Federal Register notice of application (2015-07-16) states: 'The Natchez Pipeline will provide up to 48,300 Dekatherms per day at an estimated cost of $66.2 million' -- this is where GEM's current $66,200,000 value traces to, and it is explicitly labeled an ESTIMATE filed with the initial 2015 application, before construction. Two independent 2017 in-service sources instead report the actual cost: Business Wire (company's own release, 2017-04-04, via Wayback): 'The project was financed with $60 million of 3.77% senior secured notes due June 30, 2031 ... issued ... in September 2016.' NGI (independent trade press, 2017-04-06, via Wayback): 'American Midstream said the $60 million pipeline, with capacity to deliver 50,000 Dth/d, has been placed into service.' Both post-construction sources agree independently on $60 million, materially below the pre-construction $66.2M estimate GEM currently carries -- a real, sourced disagreement, not noise. NOTE (not a separate concern, folded in here since it is the same estimate-vs-actual pattern): Capacity shows the same estimate/actual split but in GEM's favor rather than against it -- the 2015 FERC estimate was 48,300 Dth/d (~48 MMcf/d, matching GEM's current Capacity=48.00 MMcf/d) while the 2017 in-service announcements (both Business Wire and NGI) instead state 50,000 Dth/d design capacity. But Black Bear Transmission's CURRENT operating page (blackbearllc.com/natural-gas-transmission, read live) lists Midla's present capacity as '48 MDth/d capacity, 26 MDth/d FT contracts' -- i.e., today's authoritative operator-of-record figure matches GEM's 48.00 exactly. Given the current-operator source outranks the two 2017 launch-announcement figures for a present-day Capacity cell, I am NOT flagging Capacity as a concern -- it is confirmed by the two closest-to-now, most authoritative sources (2015 FERC estimate + present-day operator data), with the 2017 announcements as an interim outlier noted here for the record.
